We have assembled a portfolio of royalties which entitles us to payments based directly on the top-line sales of many of the industry’s leading therapies, which includes royalties on more than 35 commercial products, including Vertex’s Trikafta and Alyftrek, GSK’s Trelegy, Biogen’s Tysabri and Spinraza, Roche’s Evrysdi, Astellas and Pfizer’s Xtandi, Johnson & Johnson’s Tremfya, AbbVie and Johnson & Johnson’s Imbruvica, Servier’s Voranigo, Gilead’s Trodelvy, Amgen’s Imdelltra and Alnylam’s Amvuttra, among others, and 16 development-stage product candidates.

In October 2026, Revolution Medicines announced that the European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) had adopted a positive opinion of Rasonque for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy.

The study met its primary endpoint at a pre-specified interim analysis, demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in overall survival, and also met secondary endpoints of progression-free survival and objective response rate.

In July 2026, Pharvaris announced that the FDA accepted its New Drug Application (“NDA”) for deucrictibant immediate-release for the on-demand treatment of HAE attacks and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (“PDUFA”) date of April 23, 2027.
In September 2026, Teva announced positive topline results from an ongoing Phase 2a study of TEV-’408, an anti-IL-15 antibody, in adults with celiac disease.

In August 2026, Teva announced that the FDA accepted its NDA for ecopipam for the treatment of pediatric Tourette syndrome and granted the application Priority Review with a PDUFA date late in the first quarter of 2027.

In August 2026, Zenas BioPharma announced that the FDA accepted for review its Biologics License Application for obexelimab for the treatment of immunoglobulin G4-related disease and assigned a PDUFA target action date of May 27, 2027.
A royalty is the contractual right to a percentage of top-line sales from a licensee’s use of a product, technology or intellectual property.
A synthetic royalty is the contractual right to a percentage of top-line sales by the developer or marketer of a therapy in exchange for funding.
